children.value: > Fact From Story: The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.

> > Fact From Story: Other Google technologies, like “Featured Snippets” where Google algorithmically extracts answers from webpages, were also cited as shifting traffic away from publishers’ websites.

> > > Fact From Story: The lawsuit reiterates this concern, claiming that Google’s recent advances in AI-based search were implemented with “the goal of discouraging end-users from visiting the websites of Class members who are part of the digital news and publishing line of commerce.”
> > > Fact From Story: In the complaint, Helena World Chronicle argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.”
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Discouraging users from visiting a website results in a loss of ad revenue for the website.
> > Fact From Story: The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.
> > > Fact From Story: Google compiled this massive database by extracting information from Publishers’ websites.
> > > Fact From Story: By 2020, the Knowledge Graph had grown to 500 billion facts about 5 billion entities.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Extracting information from a publisher's website without permission is siphoning off their content.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Shifting traffic away from a website decreases its ad revenue.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Actions that are anticompetitive are harmful to free trade and the economy.
